gap: No result ChatGPT got compares an extender's body size with a 14-inch laptop's lid. Measured that way, a laptop size inside the maker's fit range does not mean the screen fits the lid. On a 14-inch MacBook Pro lid (31.26 × 22.12 cm, Apple), the Duex Max body (32.0 × 22.6 cm, reviewers' figures) is 0.74 cm wider and 0.48 cm taller. The folded Trio 3 Pro (34 × 22.4 cm, Macworld) is 2.74 cm wider, and Mobile Pixels' own fit range for the Trio 3 Pro is 15–16-inch laptops, so a 14-inch laptop is outside it.
standout_why: I compared against the two cited rivals, itechguides '15 Best Laptop Screen Extenders for 2026' and The Office Journal 'Best USB-C Laptop Screen Extenders', plus the top result, The Office Journal 'Best 14-Inch Laptop Screen Extenders'. All three give only laptop-diagonal fit ranges such as '13-17 inch' or '14-17.3 inch', taken from Amazon listings. They give no body or lid dimensions. The Office Journal 14-inch page says only 'verify clip fit against your specific laptop generation', and itechguides tells readers to 'measure the lid' but gives no figures. Our own two pages, best-laptop-screen-extender and best-laptop-screen-extender-under-300, give fit ranges with whose range each is: Trio 3 Pro 15–16 (Mobile Pixels), Aura Dual Boost 14 12–16 (Aura), FOPO S7 12–17.3. Neither gives a body size, a lid size or an overhang. The under-$300 page already says each driver-free screen needs its own video connection and gives the base M1–M3 MacBook limits, so neither is new.
decides: It backs the Duex Max DS as the one-screen pick for a 14-inch laptop, with a footnote: the body is about 7 mm wider than a 14-inch MacBook Pro lid, so it sits flush with a small overhang. Help Desk Geek says smaller laptops can't mount it properly 'because of the size of the panel construction', and Keith Wee ran it on a MacBook Pro 14. It argues against putting ChatGPT's two-screen pick, the Trio 3 Pro, in a 14-inch table on fit grounds. Mobile Pixels' range excludes 14-inch, and its folded body is about 2.7 cm wider than a 14-inch MacBook Pro lid, even though Macworld ran it on one. If a Mobile Pixels screen is used for two added screens, the row should say the 14-inch fit comes from Macworld's test, not from the maker. That leaves our FOPO S7 (FOPO range 12–17.3, per our page) and Aura's Dual Boost 14 (Aura range 12–16) as two-screen rows whose maker range includes 14-inch. I could not get the FOPO S7's body size, so its lid fit is not measured.
